# hubcap

A [dol](https://github.com/i2mint/dol) (i.e. dict-like) interface to github

To install:	`pip install hubcap`

# Examples

## Basics

The simplest facade to github data.

Interact with github like you’d interact with a `dict` object.

Warning: You’ll need to have a github api token (google it if you don’t have one;
it’s easy to get). You’ll have to specify this token when making hubcap objects,
or put it in an environmental variable under the name `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `HUBCAP_GITHUB_TOKEN`
(useful since github actions doesn’t allow you to have env variables starting with `GITHUB`).

```python
>>> s = GitHubReader('thorwhalen')  # connnecting to a particular user/organization
>>> list(s)
['agen',
 'aix',
 ...
 'viral',
 'wealth',
 'wrapt']
>>> 'a_non_existing_repository_name' in s
False
>>> 'hubcap' in s  # of course, this will be true, it's what you're using now!
True
>>> repo = s['hubcap']
>>> list(repo)
['master']
>>> branch = repo['master']
>>> list(branch)
['/.gitattributes',
 '/.github/',
 '/.gitignore',
 ...
 '/hubcap/',
 '/misc/',
 '/pyproject.toml',
 '/tests/']
>>> content = branch['/pyproject.toml']
>>> print(content[:14].decode())
[build-system]
```

## hub function

The high level function `hub` is the simplest way to get started. It’s a
function that takes a path to a github resource and returns a mapping to that
resource. The mapping is lazy, so it’s only when you access a key that the
resource is actually fetched from github.

```python
>>> repositories = hub('thorwhalen')
>>> 'hubcap' in repositories
True
>>> hubcap_repo = repositories['hubcap']
>>>
>>> repo = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap')
>>> 'master' in repo
True
>>> master_files = repo['master']
>>>
>>> files = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap/master')
>>> '/README.md' in files
True
>>> '/hubcap/' in files
True
>>> hubcap_files = files['/hubcap/']
>>> '/hubcap/base.py' in hubcap_files
True
```

### Access issues

```python
>>> issues = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap/issues')
>>> 3 in issues  # there's a "number 3" issue
True
>>> issue = issues[3]
>>> issue.title
'Test Issue'
>>> issue.body
'This is just a test issue to test that hubcap can see it.\r\n'
>>> issue.comments  # meaning "number of comments"
1
```

### Access discussions

```python
>>> discussions = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap/discussions')
>>> # get a list of discussion (keys)
>>> list(discussions)
[2, ...]
>>> # the discussion 2 should be included in that list
>>> 2 in discussions
True
>>> discussion = discussions[2]
>>> discussion
{'number': 2,
 'title': 'Root interface of hubcap',
 'body': 'Every time I need to do something with `hubcap` ...',
 'author': {'login': 'thorwhalen'},
 'createdAt': '2023-11-07T09:30:59Z',
 'updatedAt': '2023-12-05T08:25:39Z',
 'comments': [{'body': 'Further it would be nice if we ...',
   'author': 'thorwhalen',
   'replies': []}]}
>>> discussion['title']
'Root interface of hubcap'
```

Here’s a nice trick for those want to download a discussion in a nice readable format,
for you, or some AI, to look through.

```python
>>> from hubcap import create_markdown_from_jdict
>>> markdown_string = create_markdown_from_jdict(discussion)
>>> print(markdown_string)
# Root interface of hubcap

Every time I need to do something with `hubcap` I need to look up how it works again. 

That's negative points
```

## GithubReader

One of the main classes is `GithubReader`. It’s a mapping that connects to a
github user or organization, and returns a mapping of repositories. The
repositories are also mappings, that return mappings of branches, and so on.

```python
>>> from hubcap import GithubReader
>>> s = GithubReader('thorwhalen')  # connnecting to a particular user/organization
>>> list(s)
['agen',
 'aix',
 ...
 'viral',
 'wealth',
 'wrapt']
>>> 'a_non_existing_repository_name' in s
False
>>> 'hubcap' in s  # of course, this will be true, it's what you're using now!
True
>>> repo = s['hubcap']
>>> list(repo)
['master']
>>> branch = repo['master']
>>> list(branch)
['/.gitattributes', '/.github/', '/.gitignore', ...
'/hubcap/', '/misc/', '/pyproject.toml', '/tests/']
>>> content = branch['/pyproject.toml']
>>> print(content[:14].decode())
[build-system]

>>> from hubcap import get_repository_info
>>> info = get_repository_info('thorwhalen/hubcap')
>>> list(info)
['name', 'full_name', 'description', 'stargazers_count',
'forks_count', 'watchers_count', 'html_url', 'last_commit_date']
>>> info['name']
'hubcap'
>>> info['html_url']
'https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap'
>>> info['stargazers_count'] >= 1
True
```

You also have other useful objects, like `Issues`, `IssueComments`, `Discussions`, etc.

## Cached Repository Artifacts

Hubcap provides a convenient caching mechanism for repository artifacts like info, discussions, and issues. This allows you to work with GitHub data locally without repeatedly fetching from the API.

### Using local_repo_artifacts

The `local_repo_artifacts` object provides mapping interfaces to cached repository data:

```python
from hubcap import local_repo_artifacts

# Access cached repository info
info = local_repo_artifacts.info["thorwhalen/hubcap"]
print(info["name"])  # 'hubcap'
print(info["stargazers_count"])  # Number of stars

# Access cached discussions
discussions = local_repo_artifacts.discussions["thorwhalen/hubcap"]
for discussion_number in discussions:
    discussion = discussions[discussion_number]
    print(f"Discussion {discussion_number}: {discussion['title']}")

# Access cached issues
issues = local_repo_artifacts.issues["thorwhalen/hubcap"]
for issue_number in issues:
    issue = issues[issue_number]
    print(f"Issue {issue_number}: {issue.title}")
```

### Controlling cache behavior

You can control whether to use cached data or fetch fresh data:

```python
from hubcap import LocalRepoArtifacts

# Use cached data (default)
cached_artifacts = LocalRepoArtifacts(refresh=False)
info = cached_artifacts.info["thorwhalen/hubcap"]  # Uses cache if available

# Always fetch fresh data and update cache
fresh_artifacts = LocalRepoArtifacts(refresh=True)
info = fresh_artifacts.info["thorwhalen/hubcap"]  # Always fetches from GitHub
```

### Direct caching with Discussions and Issues

You can also enable caching directly when creating `Discussions` or `Issues` objects:

```python
from hubcap import Discussions, Issues

# Enable caching for discussions
discussions = Discussions("thorwhalen/hubcap", cache=True, refresh=False)
discussion_2 = discussions[2]  # Cached after first access

# Enable caching for issues
issues = Issues("thorwhalen/hubcap", cache=True, refresh=True)
issue_4 = issues[4]  # Always fetches fresh and updates cache
```

### Cache location

The cache is stored in your system’s application data directory:

- On Linux/Mac: `~/.local/share/hubcap/repos/{org}/{repo}/`
- On Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hubcap\repos\{org}\{repo}\`

Each artifact type has its own subdirectory:

- Info: `info.json` (single file per repo)
- Discussions: `discussions/{number}.json` (one file per discussion)
- Issues: `issues/{number}.json` (one file per issue)

You can customize the cache location with the `HUBCAP_DATA_FOLDER` environment variable.

# Recipes

## Clone to temp folder and get store (mapping) of files

```python
from hubcap import git_clone, git_wiki_clone
from dol import TextFiles, filt_iter, Pipe

repo_py_files = Pipe(git_clone, TextFiles, filt_iter(filt=lambda x: x.endswith(".py")))
repo_wiki_files = Pipe(git_wiki_clone, TextFiles)
```

```python
py_files = repo_py_files("i2mint/dol")
len(py_files)
# 37
```

```python
wiki_files = repo_wiki_files("i2mint/dol")
list(wiki_files)
# ['Recipes.md',
#  'Critiques-and-their-comebacks.md',
#  'Home.md',
#  'Mapping-Views.md']
```

# Licensing

hubcap itself is **Apache-2.0** (see `LICENSE`).

One dependency is not permissively licensed: **PyGithub** ships a single
`License :: OSI Approved :: GNU Library or Lesser General Public License (LGPL)`
classifier. This is a knowing, recorded decision rather than an oversight —
hubcap *is* a `dol` interface to the GitHub API, so PyGithub is load-bearing and
its objects are part of hubcap’s public surface. The full reasoning, and the
conditions under which the decision should be revisited, live in
`[tool.wads.licence]` in `pyproject.toml`.

What this means in practice: importing hubcap does not change the licence of
your code, but `pip install hubcap` puts an LGPL library in your environment.
If you **redistribute** a bundled/frozen artifact (PyInstaller and friends)
rather than letting pip install PyGithub as a separate, replaceable
distribution, the LGPL relinking obligations are yours to honour.

## Snapshot orgs: issues, PRs, discussions

```python
from hubcap.snapshot import snapshot_github
snapshot_github(["my-org"], store="my_snapshot")  # markdown + index.jsonl + raw.jsonl
```

Incremental: re-runs fetch only items updated since the last run. Seams: `client=` (data source), `store=` (any `MutableMapping`), `render=` (markdown strategy).

# hubcap.actions

GitHub Actions and CI status utilities.

This module provides functions for checking GitHub Actions workflow status and CI results.

### Functions

| [`actions_info`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.actions_info)([repo, per_page, token])           | Github actions runs info: dataframe of workflow runs sorted by last updated.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ci_status`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.ci_status)([user, hours_ago, token])             | Get a dict of CI conclusions for all recently updated repos for a user/org.    |
| [`date_selection_lidx`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.date_selection_lidx)(df[, hours_ago, ...])       | Filter DataFrame rows by date threshold.                                       |
| [`get_action_ci_status`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.get_action_ci_status)(repos[, hours_ago, token]) | Get a table of CI status for repositories.                                     |
| [`get_headers`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.get_headers)(token)                              | Get HTTP headers for GitHub API requests.                                      |
| [`get_last_build_status`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.get_last_build_status)([repo, token])            | Check the most recent GitHub Actions status of a repo.                         |
| [`get_token`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.get_token)([token, environ_name])                | Resolves token from parameter or environment variable.                         |
| [`repos_info`](_autosummary/hubcap.actions.html.md#hubcap.actions.repos_info)([user, token])                       | List repos and their info as a DataFrame.                                      |

### hubcap.actions.actions_info(repo='thorwhalen/graze', per_page=10, token=None, \*\*params)

Github actions runs info: dataframe of workflow runs sorted by last updated.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** – Repository in ‘owner/repo’ format
  * **per_page** – Number of workflow runs to retrieve
  * **token** – GitHub API token
  * **\*\*params** – Additional query parameters
* **Returns:**
  DataFrame of workflow runs with columns like ‘id’, ‘name’,
  : ’status’, ‘conclusion’, ‘created_at’, ‘updated_at’, etc.
* **Return type:**
  pd.DataFrame

### Example

```pycon
>>> actions = actions_info('i2mint/mongodol')
>>> actions.shape
(10, 30)
>>> list(actions.columns[:5])
['id', 'name', 'node_id', 'head_branch', 'head_sha']
```

### hubcap.actions.ci_status(user='thorwhalen', hours_ago=24, token=None, \*\*params)

Get a dict of CI conclusions for all recently updated repos for a user/org.

* **Parameters:**
  * **user** – GitHub username or organization name
  * **hours_ago** – Only check repos updated within this many hours ago
  * **token** – GitHub API token
  * **\*\*params** – Additional parameters for repos_info
* **Returns:**
  Mapping of ‘owner/repo’ names to their CI conclusions
* **Return type:**
  [*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### Example

```pycon
>>> statuses = ci_status('i2mint', hours_ago=24)
>>> statuses
{'i2mint/py2mqtt': 'failure',
 'i2mint/mongodol': 'success',
 'i2mint/dol': 'success'}
```

### hubcap.actions.date_selection_lidx(df, hours_ago=24, date_column='updated_at', op=<built-in function gt>)

Filter DataFrame rows by date threshold.

Helper function to create a boolean index for rows with dates that satisfy
a comparison operator relative to a threshold.

* **Parameters:**
  * **df** – DataFrame with a date column
  * **hours_ago** – Number of hours ago for the threshold
  * **date_column** – Name of the column containing dates
  * **op** – Comparison operator (default: operator.gt for “greater than”)
* **Returns:**
  Boolean array for indexing rows that match the criteria
* **Return type:**
  np.ndarray

### Example

```pycon
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({'updated_at': ['2024-01-01', '2024-01-15']})
>>> recent_idx = date_selection_lidx(df, hours_ago=24*30)
>>> df.iloc[recent_idx]
```

### hubcap.actions.get_action_ci_status(repos, hours_ago=8760, token=None)

Get a table of CI status for repositories.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repos** – DataFrame with repository info (must have ‘full_name’ and ‘updated_at’ columns)
  * **hours_ago** – Only check repos updated within this many hours ago
  * **token** – GitHub API token
* **Returns:**
  Series mapping repo names to their CI conclusions
* **Return type:**
  pd.Series

### Example

```pycon
>>> repos = repos_info('i2mint')
>>> ci_statuses = get_action_ci_status(repos, hours_ago=24*30)
>>> ci_statuses
full_name
i2mint/dol        success
i2mint/creek      success
dtype: object
```

### hubcap.actions.get_headers(token)

Get HTTP headers for GitHub API requests.

* **Parameters:**
  **token** – GitHub API token
* **Returns:**
  Headers dictionary with Authorization and Accept fields
* **Return type:**
  [*dict*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### hubcap.actions.get_last_build_status(repo='thorwhalen/graze', token=None, \*\*params)

Check the most recent GitHub Actions status of a repo.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** – Repository in ‘owner/repo’ format
  * **token** – GitHub API token
  * **\*\*params** – Additional query parameters
* **Returns:**
  The conclusion of the last workflow run (e.g., ‘success’,
  : ’failure’, ‘cancelled’, ‘skipped’), or None if no runs found.
* **Return type:**
  [*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) or *None*

### Example

```pycon
>>> status = get_last_build_status('thorwhalen/hubcap')
>>> status in ('success', 'failure', None)
True
```

### hubcap.actions.get_token(token=None, environ_name='GITHUB_TOKEN')

Resolves token from parameter or environment variable.

* **Parameters:**
  * **token** – GitHub API token. If None, will look in environment variable.
  * **environ_name** – Name of environment variable to check for token.
* **Returns:**
  GitHub API token
* **Return type:**
  [*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Raises:**
  [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – If token is None and environment variable is not set.

### hubcap.actions.repos_info(user='thorwhalen', token=None, \*\*params)

List repos and their info as a DataFrame.

* **Parameters:**
  * **user** – GitHub username or organization name
  * **token** – GitHub API token
  * **\*\*params** – Additional query parameters for the API call
* **Returns:**
  DataFrame with repository information, indexed by full_name
* **Return type:**
  pd.DataFrame

### Example

```pycon
>>> repos = repos_info('i2mint')
>>> repos.shape
(60, 78)
>>> list(repos.columns[:5])
['id', 'node_id', 'name', 'full_name', 'private']
```

# _autosummary/hubcap.casting.html.md

# hubcap.casting

Transformation graph for GitHub project references with flexible input handling.

This module provides automatic conversion between different representations of GitHub
projects using i2.castgraph. It integrates with hubcap’s URL parsing/generation and
supports user-configurable local project folder discovery.

## Supported Kinds

- **proj_name**: Simple project name (e.g., “dol”)
- **github_stub**: Org/repo format (e.g., “i2mint/dol”)
- **github_https_url**: HTTPS URLs (e.g., “[https://github.com/i2mint/dol](https://github.com/i2mint/dol)”)
- **github_ssh_url**: SSH URLs (e.g., “[git@github.com](mailto:git@github.com):i2mint/dol.git”)
- **local_git_folder**: Local path with .git folder
- **local_proj_folder**: Alias for local_git_folder
- **url_components**: Parsed URL components dict

## Configuration

Register your local project root folders in the hubcap config:

```pycon
>>> from hubcap.casting import register_project_root, get_project_roots
>>> register_project_root('/Users/me/projects/personal')
>>> register_project_root('/Users/me/work')
>>> get_project_roots()
['/Users/me/projects/personal', '/Users/me/work']
```

The system will search one level deep in these roots for folders containing .git.

## Usage with Ingress Decorator

```pycon
>>> from hubcap.casting import project_kinds
>>>
>>> @project_kinds.ingress('local_proj_folder')
... def process_project(project_path: str):
...     '''Accepts any project reference, gets local path.'''
...     return f"Processing {project_path}"
>>>
>>> process_project("dol")
>>> process_project("i2mint/dol")
>>> process_project("https://github.com/i2mint/dol")
```

## Direct Transformation

```pycon
>>> from hubcap.casting import normalize_project
>>>
>>> # From name to local path
>>> normalize_project("dol", to_kind='local_proj_folder')
'/Users/thorwhalen/Dropbox/py/proj/i/dol'
>>>
>>> # From URL to stub
>>> normalize_project(
...     "https://github.com/i2mint/dol/tree/master",
...     to_kind='github_stub'
... )
'i2mint/dol'
```

### hubcap.casting.normalize_project(project, , to_kind='local_proj_folder')

Normalize any project reference to the desired kind.

This allows flexible input handling - pass a project name, stub, URL, or path
and get it converted to whatever format you need.

* **Parameters:**
  * **project** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)) – Any valid project reference
  * **to_kind** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'local_proj_folder'`, `'local_git_folder'`, `'github_stub'`, `'proj_name'`, `'github_https_url'`, `'github_ssh_url'`, `'url_components'`]) – Target kind to convert to
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)
* **Returns:**
  The project reference in the desired format
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If the project cannot be found or converted

### Examples

```pycon
>>> # From simple name to path
>>> normalize_project("dol")
'/Users/thorwhalen/Dropbox/py/proj/i/dol'
```

```pycon
>>> # From URL to stub
>>> normalize_project(
...     "https://github.com/i2mint/dol/tree/master",
...     to_kind='github_stub'
... )
'i2mint/dol'
```

```pycon
>>> # From SSH URL to HTTPS URL
>>> normalize_project(
...     "git@github.com:i2mint/dol.git",
...     to_kind='github_https_url'
... )
'https://github.com/i2mint/dol'
```

Projects (folders with .git) one level below this root will be discoverable
by project name.

* **Parameters:**

* **Raises:**

### Example

```pycon
>>> register_project_root('/Users/me/projects')
>>> register_project_root('/Users/me/work/repos')
```

### hubcap.casting.set_project_roots(roots)

Replace the registered project roots with `roots`.

This is the *single write path* for the registry: `register_project_root`
and `unregister_project_root` both go through it, so anything that must
happen when the registry changes (currently, dropping the stale project
lookup cache) has exactly one place to live.

* **Parameters:**
  **roots** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The full list of project root paths to persist
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### Example

```pycon
>>> set_project_roots(['/Users/me/projects'])
```

# _autosummary/hubcap.html.md

# hubcap

The simplest facade to github data.

#### WARNING
You’ll need to have a github api token (google it if you don’t have one;
it’s easy to get). You’ll have to specify this token when making hubcap objects,
or put it in an environmental variable under the name `HUBCAP_GITHUB_TOKEN` or
`GITHUB_TOKEN`

### Example usage

### RepoReader

```pycon
>>> from hubcap import RepoReader
>>> r = RepoReader('thorwhalen/test_repo')
>>> sorted(r)
['artifacts', 'assignees', 'autolinks', 'branches', 'codescan_alerts', 'collaborators',
'comments', 'commits', 'contributors', 'deployments', 'discussions', 'downloads',
'environments', 'events', 'forks', 'git_refs', 'hooks', 'issues', 'issues_comments',
'issues_events', 'labels', 'languages', 'milestones', 'network_events',
'notifications', 'pending_invitations', 'projects', 'pulls', 'pulls_comments',
'pulls_review_comments', 'releases', 'repository_advisories', 'secrets',
'self_hosted_runners', 'stargazers', 'stargazers_with_dates', 'stats_contributors',
'subscribers', 'tags', 'teams', 'top_paths', 'top_referrers', 'topics', 'variables',
'watchers', 'workflow_runs', 'workflows']
>>>
>>> 'issues' in r
True
>>> issues = r['issues']
>>> sorted(issues)
[4, 5]
>>> issue_obj = issues[4]
>>> issue_obj
Issue(title="Test Issue A", number=4)
>>> sorted([attr for attr in dir(issue_obj) if not attr.startswith('_')])
['CHECK_AFTER_INIT_FLAG', 'active_lock_reason', 'add_to_assignees', 'add_to_labels',
'as_pull_request', 'assignee', 'assignees', 'body', 'closed_at', 'closed_by',
'comments', 'comments_url', 'create_comment', 'create_reaction', 'created_at',
'delete_labels', 'delete_reaction', 'edit', 'etag', 'events_url', 'get__repr__',
'get_comment', 'get_comments', 'get_events', 'get_labels', 'get_reactions',
'get_timeline', 'html_url', 'id', 'labels', 'labels_url', 'last_modified', 'lock',
'locked', 'milestone', 'number', 'pull_request', 'raw_data', 'raw_headers',
'remove_from_assignees', 'remove_from_labels', 'repository', 'setCheckAfterInitFlag',
'set_labels', 'state', 'state_reason', 'title', 'unlock', 'update', 'updated_at',
'url', 'user']
>>> issue_obj.number
4
>>> issue_obj.state
'open'
>>> issue_obj.labels
[Label(name="documentation"), Label(name="enhancement")]
>>> # title of issue
>>> issue_obj.title
'Test Issue A'
>>> # content of issue
>>> issue_obj.body
'Contents of Test Issue A'
>>>
>>> issue_obj.comments
2
>>>
>>> list(issue_obj.get_comments())
[IssueComment(user=NamedUser(login="thorwhalen"), id=1801792378),
IssueComment(user=NamedUser(login="thorwhalen"), id=1801792855)]
>>> issue_comment = issue_obj.get_comment(1801792378)
>>> issue_comment.body
'Comment 1 of Test Issue A'
>>>
>>> 'discussions' in r
True
>>> discussions = r['discussions']
>>> sorted(discussions)
[1, 2, 3]
```

## hub function

The high level function `hub` is the simplest way to get started. It’s a
function that takes a path to a github resource and returns a mapping to that
resource. The mapping is lazy, so it’s only when you access a key that the
resource is actually fetched from github.

```pycon
>>> repositories = hub('thorwhalen')
>>> 'hubcap' in repositories
True
>>> hubcap_repo = repositories['hubcap']
>>>
>>> repo = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap')
>>> 'master' in repo
True
>>> master_files = repo['master']
>>>
>>> files = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap/master')
>>> '/README.md' in files
True
>>> '/hubcap/' in files
True
>>> hubcap_files = files['/hubcap/']
>>> '/hubcap/base.py' in hubcap_files
True
```

### Access issues

```pycon
>>> issues = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap/issues')
>>> 3 in issues  # there's a "number 3" issue
True
>>> issue = issues[3]
>>> issue.title
'Test Issue'
>>> issue.body
'This is just a test issue to test that hubcap can see it.\r\n'
>>> issue.comments  # meaning "number of comments"
2
```

### Access discussions

```pycon
>>> discussions = hub('thorwhalen/hubcap/discussions')
>>> 2 in discussions
True
>>> discussion = discussions[2]
>>> discussion['title']
'Root interface of hubcap'
```

### GithubReader

One of the main classes is `GithubReader`. It’s a mapping that connects to a
github user or organization, and returns a mapping of repositories. The
repositories are also mappings, that return mappings of branches, and so on.

```pycon
>>> from hubcap import GithubReader
>>> s = GithubReader('thorwhalen')  # connnecting to a particular user/organization
>>> list(s)
['agen',
 'aix',
 ...
 'viral',
 'wealth',
 'wrapt']
>>> 'a_non_existing_repository_name' in s
False
>>> 'hubcap' in s  # of course, this will be true, it's what you're using now!
True
>>> repo = s['hubcap']
>>> 'master' in repo and 'gh-pages' in repo
True
>>> branch = repo['master']
>>> list(branch)
['/.gitattributes', '/.github/', '/.gitignore', ...]
>>> content = branch['/pyproject.toml']
>>> print(content[:14].decode())
[build-system]
```

```pycon
>>> from hubcap import get_repository_info
>>> info = get_repository_info('thorwhalen/hubcap')
>>> list(info)
['name', 'full_name', 'description', ...]
>>> info['name']
'hubcap'
>>> info['html_url']
'https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap'
>>> info['stargazers_count'] >= 1
True
```

You also have other useful objects, like `Issues`, `IssueComments`, `Discussions`, etc.

### hubcap.repo_slurp.add_offset_to_headers(markdown_text, offset=0)

Returns the same text but where the (markdown) headers have been offset by `offset`.

It works by adding `offset` number of ‘#’ to the start of each header line.

If the offset causes a header level to become zero or negative, it is ignored (remains the same).

Comments (lines starting with ‘#’) in code blocks are not affected by the offset.

```pycon
>>> add_offset_to_headers("## Header 1\n\n### Header 2\n\n#### Header 3", 1)
'### Header 1\n\n#### Header 2\n\n##### Header 3'
>>> add_offset_to_headers("## Header 1\n\n### Header 2\n\n#### Header 3", -1)
'# Header 1\n\n## Header 2\n\n### Header 3'
```

Note that comments in code blocks are not affected:

```pycon
>>> add_offset_to_headers("```\n# Not a header\n```", 1)
'```\n# Not a header\n```'
```

```pycon
>>> add_offset_to_headers("## Header 1\n\n```\n# Not a header\n```\n\n### Header 2", 1)
'### Header 1\n\n```\n# Not a header\n```\n\n#### Header 2'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hubcap.repo_slurp.text_from_mapping(mapping, kv_to_text=<function kv_to_python_aware_markdown>)

Creates a string from a given mapping with string keys and values using a formatting function.

* **Parameters:**
  * **mapping** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)) – A mapping with string keys and values.
  * **kv_to_text** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`KT`, `VT`], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Function that takes a key and value and returns a string.
* **Returns:**
  A string aggregate of the values of the mapping.
* **Return type:**
  [*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### Example

```pycon
>>> example_mapping = {
...     "apple.txt": "Crumble",
...     "tit.md": "For tat.",
...     "state.cfg": "Of the art."
... }
>>> example_kv_to_text = lambda k, v: f"## {k}\n```\n{v}\n```"
>>> print(text_from_mapping(example_mapping, example_kv_to_text))
## apple.txt
```

```text
Crumble
```

## tit.md

```text
For tat.
```

## state.cfg

```text
Of the art.
```


# _autosummary/hubcap.snapshot.html.md

# hubcap.snapshot

Incremental snapshot of GitHub orgs: issues, PRs and discussions with all comments.

`snapshot_github(["my-org"], store=...)` writes, per item, a markdown file with front
matter, plus `index.jsonl` (one line per item) and `raw.jsonl` (the API payloads).
Re-runs are cheap: a per-repo `updated_at` high-water mark is kept in a *state* store
and only newer items are fetched.

Three seams, each one keyword argument:

- `client`: where the data comes from (default [`GithubClient`](_autosummary/hubcap.snapshot.html.md#hubcap.snapshot.GithubClient), REST +
  GraphQL via `requests`). Anything with the same four methods works, which is also
  how the tests run offline.
- `store`: where files go, any `MutableMapping[str, str]` (default: a folder, via
  `dol.TextFiles`).
- `render`: `(kind, repo, item) -> str`, the markdown strategy.

```pycon
>>> render_markdown('issues', 'o/r', {'number': 1, 'title': 'T', 'body': 'B',
...     'state': 'open', 'user': {'login': 'u'}, 'updated_at': '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z',
...     'html_url': 'u', 'comments_data': []}).startswith('---')
True
```

### Functions

| [`render_markdown`](_autosummary/hubcap.snapshot.html.md#hubcap.snapshot.render_markdown)(kind, repo, item)                 | Markdown with front matter for one issue, PR or discussion (default renderer).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`snapshot_github`](_autosummary/hubcap.snapshot.html.md#hubcap.snapshot.snapshot_github)(targets, \*[, store, state, ...]) | Snapshot every repo of the given orgs (`"org"`) or repos (`"org/name"`).         |

### Classes

| [`GithubClient`](_autosummary/hubcap.snapshot.html.md#hubcap.snapshot.GithubClient)([token, session])     | The default client: REST for issues/PRs, GraphQL for discussions.                          |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SnapshotClient`](_autosummary/hubcap.snapshot.html.md#hubcap.snapshot.SnapshotClient)(\*args, \*\*kwargs) | What [`snapshot_github()`](_autosummary/hubcap.snapshot.html.md#hubcap.snapshot.snapshot_github) needs from GitHub. |

  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### issues(repo, since)

Issues *and* PRs (PRs carry a `pull_request` key) updated since *since*.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### repos(org)

* **Return type:**

### hubcap.snapshot.snapshot_github(targets, \*, store='github_snapshot', state=None, client=None, render=<function render_markdown>, kinds=('issues', 'pulls', 'discussions'), full=False)

Snapshot every repo of the given orgs (`"org"`) or repos (`"org/name"`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – a `MutableMapping[str, str]` or a folder path (default folder
    `github_snapshot`). Keys are `<repo>/<kind>/<number>.md` plus
    `raw/<repo>/<kind>/<number>.json`, `index.jsonl` and `raw.jsonl`.
  * **state** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)]) – where the per-repo `updated_at` marks live; defaults to a
    `.state.json` entry inside *store*, so the folder is self-contained.
  * **full** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – ignore the marks and refetch everything.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]
* **Returns:**
  counts of items written per kind.

The state mark is advanced only after a repo’s items were all written, so a crash
re-fetches (idempotently overwriting) rather than skipping.

### *class* hubcap.tools.LocalRepoArtifacts(refresh=False)

Bases: `KvReader`

Provides mapping interfaces to locally cached repository artifacts.

This class gives you access to cached repository information, discussions, and
issues through simple mapping interfaces. Data is cached locally and can be
refreshed on demand.

* **Parameters:**
  **refresh** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, always fetch fresh data from GitHub and update cache.
  If False, use cached data when available.

#### info

Mapping interface to repository info (info.json for each repo)

#### discussions

Mapping interface to repository discussions

#### issues

Mapping interface to repository issues

#### ci

Mapping interface to repository CI (GitHub Actions) information

### Example

```pycon
>>> artifacts = LocalRepoArtifacts(refresh=False)
>>> # List available artifact types
>>> list(artifacts)
['info', 'discussions', 'issues', 'ci']
>>> # Access via attribute
>>> info = artifacts.info['thorwhalen/hubcap']
>>> # Or via mapping interface
>>> info = artifacts['info']['thorwhalen/hubcap']
>>> # Get cached discussions
>>> discussions = artifacts.discussions['thorwhalen/hubcap']
>>> # Access a specific discussion
>>> discussion_2 = discussions[2]
>>> # Get cached issues
>>> issues = artifacts.issues['thorwhalen/hubcap']
>>> # Get CI info
>>> ci_info = artifacts.ci['thorwhalen/hubcap']
>>> ci_info['current_state']  # True (success), False (failure), or None
True
```

The cache is stored in: {app_data_dir}/repos/{org}/{repo}/{artifact_type}/
For example:

> - Info: ~/.local/share/hubcap/repos/thorwhalen/hubcap/info.json
> - Discussions: ~/.local/share/hubcap/repos/thorwhalen/hubcap/discussions/1.json
> - Issues: ~/.local/share/hubcap/repos/thorwhalen/hubcap/issues/4.json
> - CI: ~/.local/share/hubcap/repos/thorwhalen/hubcap/ci_info.json

### hubcap.tools.get_author_commits(repo, author_email, days_range)

Fetches GitHub commits for a specific author within a given date range.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo_name** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The repo_owner/repo_name in the format for a repo.
  * **author_email** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The email address of the author to filter commits by.
  * **days_range** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple) | [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – The date range for the commits.
    If an int, it’s the number of days back from today.
    If a tuple, it’s (start_date_str, end_date_str) in ‘YYYY-MM-DD’ format (inclusive).
* **Returns:**
  A list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a commit
  : and contains ‘sha’, ‘message’, ‘author_name’, ‘author_email’, ‘commit_date’.
    Returns an empty list if no commits are found or an error occurs.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### hubcap.tools.get_ci_info(repo, , refresh=False, token=None)

Get CI (GitHub Actions) info for a repository, with caching.

Fetches the most recent GitHub Actions workflow runs and returns comprehensive
info along with the current CI state. Uses actions_info which gets runs sorted
by last updated, so we get the most recent regardless of time period.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Repository in ‘owner/repo’ format
  * **refresh** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, fetches fresh data. If False, uses cached data when available.
  * **token** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – GitHub API token (optional, uses environment variable if not provided)
* **Returns:**
  Contains ‘actions’ (list of workflow runs) and ‘current_state’ (bool/None).
  : ’current_state’ is True for success, False for failure, None for no CI or cancelled.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### Example

```pycon
>>> ci = get_ci_info('thorwhalen/hubcap')
>>> ci['current_state']
True
>>> ci['actions'][0]['conclusion']
'success'
```

### hubcap.tools.notebook_to_markdown(notebook_path, output_dir=None, repo_root_url=None, , image_relative_dir='')

Convert a Jupyter notebook to Markdown and optionally post-process the output.

* **Parameters:**
  * **notebook_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Path to the Jupyter notebook.
  * **output_dir** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Directory where the Markdown file will be written.
    If None, the Markdown is returned as a string.
  * **repo_root_url** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Root URL for replacing relative paths in the Markdown.
  * **image_relative_dir** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The (relative) directory where the images should be saved.
* **Returns:**
  The Markdown content, optionally post-processed.
* **Return type:**
  [*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

Usage Examples

### Convert a notebook to Markdown and return as a string

```pycon
>>> markdown_string = notebook_to_markdown(
    notebook_path="example_notebook.ipynb",
    output_dir=None,  # Do not save to a file
    repo_root_url="https://github.com/username/repo/blob/main/",
    image_relative_dir="images"
)
```

### Post-process directly from a notebook file

```pycon
>>> notebook_to_markdown = post_process_markdown_generated_from_notebook(
    md_src="example_notebook.ipynb",
    repo_root_url="https://github.com/username/repo/blob/main/"
)
```

#### get_value(path, on_error=<function raise_on_error>, \*, sep=None, key_transformer=None, get_value=functools.partial(<function defaulted_itemgetter>, default={}), caught_errors=(<class 'Exception'>, ))

Get elements of a mapping through a path to be called recursively.

* **Parameters:**
  * **obj** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – The object to get the path from
  * **path** – The path to get
  * **on_error** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The error handler to use (default: raise_on_error)
  * **sep** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Determines a path is transforms into a tuple of keys.
    If it’s a string, `lambda path: path.split(sep)` is used.
    If not, it should be a function which takes in a path object and returns an iterable of keys.
  * **key_transformer** – A function to transform the keys of the path
  * **get_value** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)) – A function to get the value of a key in a mapping
  * **caught_errors** – The errors to catch (default: Exception)

It will

- split a path into keys (if sep is given, or if path is a string, will use ‘.’ as a separator by default)
- if key_transformer is given, apply to each key
- consider string keys that are numeric as ints (convenient for lists)
- get items also as attributes (attributes are checked for first for string keys)
- catch all exceptions (that are subclasses of `Exception`)

```pycon
>>> class A:
...      an_attribute = 42
>>> path_get([1, [4, 5, {'a': A}], 3], [1, 2, 'a', 'an_attribute'])
42
```

By default, if `path` is a string, it will be split on `sep`,
which is `'.'` by default.

```pycon
>>> path_get([1, [4, 5, {'a': A}], 3], '1.2.a.an_attribute')
42
```

#### NOTE
The underlying engine is `dol._paths_core.path_get_core` (shared with
`add_path_get`), but `path_get` has defaults and flexible input processing
for more convenience. For “first of several keys that exists” (not a path),
see `dol.util.chain_get`.

#### NOTE
`path_get` contains some ready-made `OnErrorType` functions in its
attributes. For example, see how we can make `path_get` have the same behavior
as `dict.get` by passing `path_get.return_none_on_error` as `on_error`:

```pycon
>>> dd = path_get({}, 'no.keys', on_error=path_get.return_none_on_error)
>>> dd is None
True
```

For example, `path_get.raise_on_error`,
`path_get.return_none_on_error`, and `path_get.return_empty_tuple_on_error`.

### hubcap.util.cached_github_object()

Returns a cached authenticated GitHub client using the default token.

### hubcap.util.create_markdown_from_discussion_jdict(jdict)

Creates a markdown representation of a discussion or issue (metadata json-dict).

Headers are used to separate the different sections.

This is meant to be applied to json exports of github discussions or issues.

#### NOTE
For issues, the ‘comments’ field is just a count (int), not the actual
comment data. For discussions, ‘comments’ is a list of comment objects with
their full data including replies.

### hubcap.util.create_markdown_from_jdict(jdict)

Creates a markdown representation of a discussion or issue (metadata json-dict).

Headers are used to separate the different sections.

This is meant to be applied to json exports of github discussions or issues.

#### NOTE
For issues, the ‘comments’ field is just a count (int), not the actual
comment data. For discussions, ‘comments’ is a list of comment objects with
their full data including replies.

### hubcap.util.ensure_folder_to_clone_into(folder_to_clone_into=None)

Return a folder to clone into. If not provided, create a temporary folder.

### hubcap.util.ensure_full_name(repo)

Ensure we have a full name (user/repo string)

```pycon
>>> ensure_full_name('https://www.github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap')
'thorwhalen/hubcap'
>>> ensure_full_name('github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap/')
'thorwhalen/hubcap'
>>> ensure_full_name('thorwhalen/hubcap')
'thorwhalen/hubcap'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hubcap.util.ensure_github_url(user_repo_str, prefix='https://github.com/')

Ensure a string to a github url

```pycon
>>> ensure_github_url('https://www.github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap')
'https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap'
>>> ensure_github_url('https://github.com/github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap/')
'https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hubcap.util.ensure_repo_obj(repo)

Ensure a Repository object.

```pycon
>>> ensure_repo_obj('thorwhalen/hubcap')
Repository(full_name="thorwhalen/hubcap")
>>> repo = ensure_repo_obj('https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap')
>>> repo
Repository(full_name="thorwhalen/hubcap")
```

And if we pass in a `Repository` object, we just get it back:

```pycon
>>> ensure_repo_obj(repo)
Repository(full_name="thorwhalen/hubcap")
```

* **Return type:**
  `Repository`

### hubcap.util.ensure_url_suffix(url)

Ensure a url suffix, that is, get rid of the (…)github.com prefix.

```pycon
>>> ensure_url_suffix('https://www.github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap/README.md')
'thorwhalen/hubcap/README.md'
>>> ensure_url_suffix('www.github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap/README.md')
'thorwhalen/hubcap/README.md'
>>> ensure_url_suffix('thorwhalen/hubcap/README.md')
'thorwhalen/hubcap/README.md'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hubcap.util.generate_github_url(components, url_type=None, , prefer_explicit_url_type=True, ignore_extra_keys=True)

Generates a GitHub URL from the provided components dictionary.

* **Parameters:**
  * **components** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'branch'`, `'issue_number'`, `'path'`, `'pr_number'`, `'repository'`, `'username'`], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – A dictionary containing the URL components.
  * **url_type** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'fully_qualified_raw'`, `'file'`, `'raw_file'`, `'tree_path'`, `'branch'`, `'issue'`, `'pull_request'`, `'releases'`, `'repository'`, `'clone_url'`]) – The type of the URL to generate.
  * **prefer_explicit_url_type** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, the url_type argument takes
    precedence over the ‘url_type’ key in components.
    This is needed because by default, `parse_github_url` includes the
    ‘url_type’ key, so if you want to easily generate a URL from its
    components, you need an easy way to tell the function to ignore that
    particular key, overriding it with the `url_type` argument.
  * **ignore_extra_keys** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – If True, extra keys in the components dictionary
* **Returns:**
  The generated GitHub URL.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If the components are insufficient to generate a URL.

### Examples

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'repository',
...     'username': 'torvalds',
...     'repository': 'linux',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux'
```

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'branch',
...     'username': 'torvalds',
...     'repository': 'linux',
...     'branch': 'master',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux/tree/master'
```

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'file',
...     'username': 'torvalds',
...     'repository': 'linux',
...     'branch': 'master',
...     'path': 'README.md',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/README.md'
```

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'raw_file',
...     'username': 'torvalds',
...     'repository': 'linux',
...     'branch': 'master',
...     'path': 'README.md',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/README.md'
```

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'issue',
...     'username': 'torvalds',
...     'repository': 'linux',
...     'issue_number': '1',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux/issues/1'
```

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'pull_request',
...     'username': 'torvalds',
...     'repository': 'linux',
...     'pr_number': '1',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux/pull/1'
```

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'releases',
...     'username': 'torvalds',
...     'repository': 'linux',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux/releases'
```

```pycon
>>> components = {
...     'url_type': 'clone_url',
...     'username': 'username',
...     'repository': 'repo',
... }
>>> generate_github_url(components)
'git@github.com:username/repo.git'
```

### hubcap.util.get_repository_info(repo, repo_info=(('name', 'name'), ('full_name', 'full_name'), ('description', 'description'), ('open_issues_count', 'open_issues_count'), ('size', 'size'), ('updated_at', 'updated_at'), ('stargazers_count', 'stargazers_count'), ('forks_count', 'forks_count'), ('watchers_count', 'watchers_count'), ('html_url', 'html_url'), ('last_commit_date', <function \_last_commit_date>)), \*, refresh=True, token=None, use_auth=True)

Get info about a repository.

```pycon
>>> info = get_repository_info('thorwhalen/hubcap')
```

This gives us a `dict` with default info fields:

```pycon
>>> list(info)
['name', 'full_name', 'description', ...]
>>> info['name']
'hubcap'
>>> info['html_url']
'https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap'
>>> info['stargazers_count'] >= 1
True
```

We can also specify a custom `repo_info` get different info.

You can specify a space separated string of repo properties:

```pycon
>>> get_repository_info('thorwhalen/hubcap', 'name html_url')
{'name': 'hubcap', 'html_url': 'https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap'}
```

Note that you have a list of valid repo properties in `constants.repo_props`,
which is dynamically generated from the `github.Repository.Repository` class:

```pycon
>>> from hubcap.constants import repo_props
>>> len(repo_props) >= 90
True
```

If you want to give the fields different names, or use a function to compute some
custom information based on the repo you can specify a  dict of
`{field: prop_spec, ...}` values where `prop_spec` is either a valid repo
property or a function to compute the value (the function needs to take a
`Repository` as its first and only required argument).

```pycon
>>> get_repository_info(
...     'thorwhalen/hubcap',
...     {'name': 'name', 'has stars': lambda repo: repo.stargazers_count > 0}
... )
{'name': 'hubcap', 'has stars': True}
```

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** (`Repository`) – Repository object or string identifier
  * **repo_info** ### hubcap.util.git(command='status', , work_tree=None, git_dir=None, suppress_errors=False)

Launch git commands.

* **Parameters:**
  * **command** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – git command (e.g. ‘status’, ‘branch’, ‘commit -m “blah”’, ‘push’, etc.)
  * **work_tree** – The work_tree directory (i.e. where the project is)
  * **git_dir** – The .git directory (usually, and by default, will be taken to be “{work_tree}/.git/”
  * **suppress_errors** – If True, suppress errors and return an empty string or None.
* **Returns:**
  What ever the command line returns (decoded to string), or an empty string/None if errors are suppressed.

### hubcap.util.git_clone(repo, clone_to_folder=None, branch=None)

Clone a GitHub repository, optionally specifying a branch.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** – Repository URL or identifier
  * **clone_to_folder** – Local folder to clone into (creates temp folder if None)
  * **branch** – Optional branch name to clone (clones default branch if None)
* **Returns:**
  Path to the cloned repository folder

### hubcap.util.github_file_contents(file_url, \*, egress=<function <lambda>>)

Fetches the contents of a file from a GitHub repository.

* **Parameters:**
  * **file_url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The URL of the file to fetch (doesn’t have to be a raw file!)
  * **egress** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)) – A function to extract the contents of the file object. By default, it
    decodes the file object’s content as UTF-8, but if it’s bytes you want,
    don’t decode those bytes, and if it’s the “file object” you want, just
    use `egress=lambda x: x`.
* **Returns:**
  The contents of the file as a string.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Raises:**
  [**Exception**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#Exception) – If the repository, file, or branch does not exist, or access is denied.

```pycon
>>> file_string = github_file_contents('https://github.com/thorwhalen/hubcap/blob/master/pyproject.toml')
>>> print(file_string[:14])
[build-system]
```

### hubcap.util.github_json_deserializer(data)

Decode JSON bytes back to Python objects.

### hubcap.util.github_json_serializer(obj)

Prepare objects for JSON serialization, handling GitHub API objects and datetime.

Handles datetime objects and other common GitHub API types by recursively
converting them to JSON-serializable types, then encoding to JSON bytes.

```pycon
>>> from datetime import datetime, timezone
>>> dt = datetime(2021, 1, 15, 22, 34, 10, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
>>> result = github_json_serializer(dt)
>>> result
b'"2021-01-15T22:34:10+00:00"'
>>> github_json_serializer({'created_at': dt, 'name': 'test'})
b'{"created_at": "2021-01-15T22:34:10+00:00", "name": "test"}'
```

### hubcap.util.parse_github_url(url, , include_url_type=True)

Parses a GitHub URL and returns a dictionary of its components.

The returned dict includes a “url_type” field that indicates the type of the URL.

* **Parameters:**
  **url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The GitHub URL to parse.
* **Returns:**
  A dictionary containing the parsed components.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If the URL cannot be parsed.

### Examples

```pycon
>>> parse_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux')
{'username': 'torvalds', 'repository': 'linux', 'url_type': 'repository'}
>>> parse_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux/tree/master')
{'username': 'torvalds', 'repository': 'linux', 'branch': 'master', 'url_type': 'branch'}
>>> parse_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/README.md')
{'username': 'torvalds', 'repository': 'linux', 'branch': 'master', 'path': 'README.md', 'url_type': 'file'}
>>> parse_github_url('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/README.md')
{'username': 'torvalds', 'repository': 'linux', 'branch': 'master', 'path': 'README.md', 'url_type': 'raw_file'}
>>> parse_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux/issues/1')
{'username': 'torvalds', 'repository': 'linux', 'issue_number': '1', 'url_type': 'issue'}
>>> parse_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux/pull/1')
{'username': 'torvalds', 'repository': 'linux', 'pr_number': '1', 'url_type': 'pull_request'}
>>> parse_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux/releases')
{'username': 'torvalds', 'repository': 'linux', 'url_type': 'releases'}
>>> parse_github_url('git@github.com:username/repo.git')
{'username': 'username', 'repository': 'repo', 'url_type': 'clone_url'}
```

### hubcap.util.replace_relative_urls(markdown_str, root_url, , relative_url_pattern='(!?\\\\[.\*?\\\\]\\\\()((?!http[s]?://|ftp://|mailto:|#|/)[^)]\*)(\\\\))|(<img\\\\s+[^>]\*src=")((?!http[s]?://|ftp://|mailto:|#|/)[^"]\*)(")')

Replace relative URLs in a markdown string with absolute URLs based on the root_url.

This is useful, for example, to solve problems like when pypi renders markdown and
images are not shown because they are relative URLs.
See [issue]()

* **Parameters:**
  * **markdown_str** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The markdown content containing URLs.
  * **root_url** ([*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The base URL to resolve relative URLs against.
* **Returns:**
  The markdown content with relative URLs replaced by absolute URLs.
* **Return type:**
  [*str*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### Examples

```pycon
>>> markdown_str = '''
... [With dot](./page)
... ![With double dot](../image.png)
... ![](relative/path/to/image.png)
... [Absolute Link](http://example.com)
... <img src="path/to/image" width="320">
... '''
>>> root_url = 'http://mysite.com/docs'
>>> print(replace_relative_urls(markdown_str, root_url))

[With dot](http://mysite.com/docs/page)
![With double dot](http://mysite.com/image.png)
![](http://mysite.com/docs/relative/path/to/image.png)
[Absolute Link](http://example.com)
<img src="http://mysite.com/docs/path/to/image" width="320">
```

### hubcap.util.transform_github_url(url, target_url_type='raw_file', \*\*extras)

Transforms a GitHub URL to another type, updating components as needed.

* **Parameters:**
  * **url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The original GitHub URL.
  * **target_url_type** ([`Literal`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)[`'fully_qualified_raw'`, `'file'`, `'raw_file'`, `'tree_path'`, `'branch'`, `'issue'`, `'pull_request'`, `'releases'`, `'repository'`, `'clone_url'`]) – The desired URL type.
  * **\*\*extras** – Additional components to update in the URL.
* **Returns:**
  The transformed GitHub URL.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If the URL cannot be parsed or transformed.

### Examples

```pycon
>>> transform_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux', 'clone_url')
'git@github.com:torvalds/linux.git'
```

```pycon
>>> transform_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/README.md', 'raw_file')
'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/README.md'
```

```pycon
>>> transform_github_url('https://github.com/torvalds/linux/issues/1', 'pull_request', pr_number='42')
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux/pull/42'
```

```pycon
>>> transform_github_url('git@github.com:torvalds/linux.git', 'file', branch='master', path='README.md')
'https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/README.md'
```
